headline: Wet, windy weekend with flood and wind alerts; drier, near-normal weather midweek.
summary: A series of Pacific storm systems keeps western Washington wet and breezy, with a strong front arriving this weekend. Next week, the storm track, the path storms usually follow, is expected to shift south of the region. Toward the end of the week, a blocking pattern, a stalled area of high pressure over the West, should keep the area mostly dry. The weekend is the main concern. Saturday night into early Sunday brings the strongest winds, with wind advisories for parts of the coast and the San Juans. Most rain falls Saturday night, and the Skokomish River, in the southern Hood Canal area, is at risk of flooding. Big surf is expected on the coast. Sunday and Monday turn showery, with temperatures near normal. Forecasters are confident about the weekend storm, and the drier midweek trend is expected, though with less detail.
changes: Compared with the early morning discussion, the possible storm-force winds on the outer coast have been replaced by wind advisories for the coast and San Juans, and the Skokomish flood risk now gets more attention. The midweek dry-out has been described more firmly as a blocking pattern, though with less specific detail.
